text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of "Lilies." Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of love.
My heart stirs with a noble theme; I recite my verses for the king; my tongue is the pen of a skilled scribe.
You are the fairest of men; grace is poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
Strap your sword to your side, O mighty one, in your glory and your majesty.
In your majesty ride out in triumph for the cause of truth and humility and righteousness; let your right hand reveal awesome deeds.
Your arrows are sharp; nations fall beneath you; they pierce the hearts of the king's enemies.
Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of justice.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.
Myrrh and aloes and cassia scent all your robes; from palaces of ivory the strings make you glad.
Daughters of kings are among your honored women; at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir.
Listen, O daughter, look and incline your ear; forget your people and your father's house.
Then the king will desire your beauty; he is your lord—bow down before him.
The daughter of Tyre will come with a gift; the richest among the people will seek your favor.

versions.text: The daughter of Tyre comes with a gift; the wealthiest of peoples seek your favor.
versions.explanation: עָם is singular ("the people"), not plural "peoples." The Hebrew phrase עֲשִׁירֵי עָם means "the rich ones of the people." The correction also keeps the future/imperfect sense of יְחַלּוּ.

versions.text: The daughter of Tyre comes with a gift; the richest among the people will seek your favor.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a single verb (יְחַלּוּ, imperfect) governing both clauses; the supplied verb in the first clause reads more smoothly if it matches the future sense of the second clause. As written, the shift from present "comes" to future "will seek" is slightly jarring when read aloud.

text: All glorious is the king's daughter within her chamber; her gown is woven with gold.
In embroidered robes she is led to the king; her virgin companions follow her, brought in to you.
They are led along with joy and rejoicing; they enter the palace of the king.
In place of your fathers your sons will stand; you will make them princes throughout all the earth.

versions.text: In place of your fathers your sons will stand; you will make them princes throughout the land.
versions.explanation: בְּכָל־הָאָרֶץ here has the universal scope typical of this royal psalm (cf. the nations in v. 6 and 18); "all the earth" better conveys the breadth than the narrower "the land."

text: I will make your name remembered through all generations; therefore the peoples will praise you forever and ever.
